sections.html:
The Register of Deeds counter is inside the Gratiot County Courthouse at 214 E Center Street in Ithaca. The phone number is 989-875-5217. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon, and closures for special occasions are posted on the department page.

This is a constitutional office, and its counter handles more than 200 kinds of paper. For a seller, the usual ones are warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, land contracts and mortgage releases. The shelves also hold powers of attorney and oil and gas leases, and filings stretch back to the 1800s. Anyone may inspect a recorded document during business hours. The same window takes passport applications until 3:30 p.m., so call first if you plan to do both errands.

Staff do not draft paperwork or give legal answers, so the deed itself is a job for an attorney or a title agent. Free public terminals sit on the courthouse's lower level and in the Treasurer's office if you want to look up a parcel yourself.

One $30 charge covers a document of any length. Cash, check or card all work. Transfer tax and a tax certificate are added where they apply, and the $30 base is set in MCL 600.2567.

Gratiot County recording and copy charges
ServiceFee
Record one deed, mortgage or instrument$30
Every added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Warranty deed or land contract tax certificate$5
Copy of a real estate record$1 per page
Certifying a copy$5 per document plus $1 per page
Name search of the real estate record$0.50 per year, minimum $5

Parcel research is priced through the Treasurer's side. Terminal printouts run $1 per page, phone lookups $3, and a written property tax and assessment report $5 per parcel. A new online account gets one free parcel lookup, and later searches on records with the same owner name stay free.

Think in $500 blocks, rounding the price up. Each block pays 55 cents to the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 to the state under MCL 207.525, for $4.30 a block. Raise the price by a single dollar past a block line and the count moves up by one. The tax is separate from the $30 filing charge.

The deed should show the whole price, or a value affidavit must be attached. The title company or closing attorney normally works out the exact figure and collects it at closing, so ask for it in writing a few days ahead.

  • County exemptions: MCL 207.505. State exemptions: MCL 207.526.
  • No state tax on a deed issued in a foreclosure or in lieu of one.
  • No state tax on a conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or grandchild.
  • No tax of either kind on a corrective quitclaim that confirms title already held.

sections.h2: When unpaid tax becomes the county's problem
sections.html:
Bills go out July 1 and December 1. A current tax is paid locally, at the township, city or village office, until the first of March next year. From that day the Gratiot County Treasurer collects it. Payoff amounts come by phone.

Unpaid balances move through a fixed schedule. They turn delinquent that first March 1, become forfeited one year later, and are foreclosed on the March 31 after that. For 2025 bills that means forfeiture on March 1, 2027 and foreclosure on March 31, 2028. Foreclosed parcels go to an online auction run through tax-sale.info.

  • Cards work for delinquent balances through Graphite, which bills 2.75% with a $1 floor and turns away American Express.
  • Neither the county nor a local treasurer answers for an escrow company that skipped a payment on a mortgaged home. If you have a mortgage, confirm the lender actually paid.
  • Since December 24, 2025 the Postal Service stamps the day mail is processed instead of the day it was dropped off, which can make a last-day envelope late. Pay a few days early or deliver by hand.

Taxes owed on the parcel do not block a listing, but they do surface at closing. The title company will ask the Treasurer for a payoff and take it out of your proceeds. If an old year is open, call the Treasurer's office early, because the amount grows as the schedule above advances and a foreclosed parcel can no longer be sold the ordinary way.

A cash buyer who skips the lender's underwriting and appraisal can often close faster, but the same tax certificate and recording steps still apply to the deed.

sections.h2: Tax certificate for a warranty deed
sections.html:
A $5 tax certificate from the Treasurer's office goes with warranty deeds, deeds containing a warranty covenant, land contracts and assignments of land contracts with a warranty clause. In MCL 211.135 the treasurer vouches that the last five years are paid and that no tax liens or tax titles hang over the land.

A quitclaim without covenants skips the step. For anything else, request the certificate early in the closing window and ask what an unpaid year would cost, because the register waits for it.

Clerks screen each document against Michigan law first. A deed that clears is given the next number, stamped with the time, scanned whole and cross indexed, and its legal description plus buyer and seller are keyed into the search system. A title company later leans on that index to follow ownership.

Township and city offices, Equalization and the Treasurer each learn of a sale from this register and use it to prepare valuations for the next tax roll. After recording, any member of the public may read or copy the deed. The office suggests double-checking a document against recording requirements before submitting it, since a deed that fails the screen comes back and your closing date slips.

sections.h2: Before you go to the counter
sections.html: Bring the signed and notarized deed, the $30 fee, any transfer tax due, and the Treasurer's tax certificate if the deed carries a warranty. If a lender is paid off at closing, the mortgage release is recorded as a separate instrument at its own fee. Most sellers never visit in person, since the title company or closing attorney files the paperwork for them. Ask them for the recording number afterward so you have proof the sale reached the public record.

Gratiot County is mostly farmland and small towns in central Michigan. Ithaca is the seat and Alma is the largest city. Population has hovered near 42,000 since 2000, and the 2025 estimate is 41,190. The median home value is $147,500, with 78.9% of homes owner occupied and median rent at $834.

faqs.q: How much does Gratiot County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30 per document, no matter the page count. Transfer tax is extra on a sale, and a warranty deed needs a $5 tax certificate.

faqs.q: What are the Gratiot County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at the courthouse, 214 E Center Street, Ithaca. Passport applications stop at 3:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Is there a card option for delinquent tax in Gratiot County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer takes cards for delinquent taxes through Graphite, which adds 2.75% with a $1 minimum. American Express is not accepted, and online payments are processed in the morning and afternoon.

faqs.q: Will the Gratiot County register write my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office prepares nothing and answers no legal questions, so hire a lawyer or title agent. Before you submit, review the deed against the recording requirements so the clerks do not have to send it back.

faqs.q: When do Gratiot County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: July 1 and December 1. If one never shows up, call the township, city or village treasurer, because the tax is still owed. Current-year tax stays payable at that local office until March 1.
